records.title: Free or reduced-fee hunting and fishing license
records.summary: Arizona gives a complimentary hunting and fishing license to Veterans with a permanent 100 percent service-connected disability, and a reduced-fee license to Veterans with a lower service-connected rating. One year of Arizona residency is required either way.
records.amount: Free at 100 percent. Up to 25 percent off otherwise.
eligibility: You have lived in Arizona for one year or more immediately before you apply
You receive US government compensation for a service-connected disability
A permanent service-connected disability rated 100 percent disabling qualifies for a complimentary license
Any other service-connected disability qualifies for a license at up to 25 percent below the full fee
details: The one-year Arizona residency requirement applies to both versions and is separate from your VA rating.
Issued by the Arizona Game and Fish Department, which asks for a copy of your VA benefits letter.
If the VA certifies your 100 percent rating as permanent and not subject to reevaluation, you do not have to recertify at renewal.

records.title: Property tax exemption for Veterans with a service-connected disability
records.summary: If the VA rates you 100 percent service-connected disabled, your property is fully exempt from Arizona property tax. Below 100 percent, you get a partial exemption scaled to your rating.
records.amount: Fully exempt at 100 percent. Below that, scaled to your rating.
eligibility: You are a Veteran discharged, separated, or released under honorable conditions from the uniformed services
The VA has assigned you a service-connected disability rating
A 100 percent rating exempts the property entirely
Below 100 percent, the exemption is the statutory amount multiplied by your rating percentage
Income and property assessment limits apply, and both are adjusted every year
details: The statute sets a base exemption amount of $4,188, which the Arizona Department of Revenue adjusts every year for inflation. The current year's figure is higher than the number written in the statute, so confirm the exact amount with your county assessor before you rely on it.
This is claimed through your county assessor, not through the state. Deadlines are set at the county level.

Arizona has amended this exemption more than once in recent sessions, including changes to how it applies to a primary residence at a 100 percent rating. Check the current statute text if your situation is close to the line.
records.agency: Arizona Department of Revenue, administered by county assessors

records.title: Military Family Relief Fund
records.summary: Arizona pays need-based financial assistance of up to $20,000 per family to service members and families affected by a death, wound, injury, or serious illness connected to military service.
records.amount: Up to $20,000 per family, based on financial need
eligibility: The service member was killed, wounded, injured, or became seriously ill, with separate subaccounts for service after September 11, 2001 and on or before that date

An Arizona connection is required: deployed from an Arizona military base, claimed Arizona as home of record, was in the Arizona National Guard at deployment, or established residency with proof of at least twelve continuous months of physical presence in Arizona before applying
Assistance is based on demonstrated financial need resulting from the military service
details: Covered uses include stipends for living expenses for up to six months for families of those killed in combat, temporary housing and medical travel for families of hospitalized service members, and other living expenses the committee approves.
IMPORTANT: the statute establishes this fund through December 31, 2026. Check whether the Legislature has extended it before relying on it.
The fund is made up of private donations, grants, and bequests, so available money varies.

records.title: Military retirement pay is fully exempt from Arizona income tax
records.summary: Arizona does not tax military retired or retainer pay. Since the 2021 tax year the full amount is subtracted from your Arizona gross income, with no cap.
records.amount: Full amount, no cap, from tax year 2021 onward
eligibility: You receive retired or retainer pay from the uniformed services of the United States
Uniformed services includes the US military, the Public Health Service Commissioned Corps, and the NOAA Commissioned Officer Corps
There is no disability rating requirement and no income test
details: The cap was removed in stages. Through 2018 the subtraction was capped at $2,500, for 2019 and 2020 it was $3,500, and from the 2021 tax year onward it is the full amount received.
This is a subtraction on your Arizona return, so you have to claim it. It is not automatic.
Arizona separately does not tax active duty military pay.

records.title: Tuition waiver scholarship at Arizona public colleges and universities
records.summary: Arizona waives tuition at its public universities and community colleges for Purple Heart recipients rated at least 50 percent disabled, and for the children and surviving spouses of service members killed in the line of duty.
records.amount: Full tuition, up to 64 credit hours at a community college
eligibility: Purple Heart recipient from the US armed forces with a VA disability rating of 50 percent or more
Or a National Guard member awarded a Purple Heart after September 11, 2001
Or the child, age 30 or younger, or the unmarried surviving spouse of a service member or first responder killed in the line of duty or who died of line-of-duty injuries
Or the child or unmarried surviving spouse of an Arizona resident Veteran or service member who suffered a post-traumatic stress injury in the line of duty and died by suicide
Purple Heart recipients with a felony conviction are not eligible
details: The same statute also covers dependents of peace officers, firefighters, correctional officers, emergency paramedics, and National Guard members killed in the line of duty.
Apply through the financial aid office of the Arizona public university or community college you plan to attend.
records.agency: Arizona Board of Regents and the community college districts

records.title: Arizona State Veteran Homes
records.summary: Arizona operates skilled nursing and long-term care homes for Veterans. The Department of Veterans Services is authorized by statute to build and run them and sets the admission rules and resident charges.
eligibility: Admission rules and resident charges are set by the Department of Veterans Services, not fixed in statute
Contact the Department directly to check eligibility and current waiting lists
details: The statute authorizes the Department to acquire property for, construct, and operate Veterans home facilities in Arizona. The detailed admission criteria live in administrative rule rather than in the statute, so the Department is the place to confirm them.
Homes operate in Phoenix and Tucson, with additional homes in Flagstaff and Yuma. Confirm current locations and availability with the Department.

records.title: Vehicle license tax and registration fee exemption
records.summary: Veterans certified by the VA at 100 percent disability and drawing compensation on that basis pay no vehicle license tax and no registration fees on one vehicle.
records.amount: No vehicle license tax or registration fees on one vehicle
eligibility: The VA has certified you as 100 percent disabled and you are drawing compensation on that basis
Covers one personally owned vehicle, or a vehicle you own with another party, and any replacement of it
You must show satisfactory proof of the certification when you first register the vehicle
A surviving spouse keeps the exemption until remarriage or death
details: This covers one vehicle at a time. Replacing that vehicle carries the exemption over; adding a second vehicle does not.
Handled by the Arizona Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Division at registration.
records.agency: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division

records.title: Arizona Veterans' Memorial Cemeteries
records.summary: Arizona establishes and operates state cemeteries for Veterans, and provides burial services there for Arizona National Guard and US Armed Forces Reserve members discharged under honorable conditions.
eligibility: Veterans, under the Department of Veterans Services rules
Members of the Arizona National Guard whose service was terminated under honorable conditions
Members of the United States armed forces reserves whose service was terminated under honorable conditions
details: The statute authorizes the Department to acquire property for, establish, and operate cemeteries for Veterans in Arizona, and specifically to provide burial services for Guard and Reserve members separated under honorable conditions.
State cemeteries operate at Sierra Vista, Camp Navajo near Flagstaff, and Marana north of Tucson. Confirm current locations and eligibility with the Department before making arrangements.

records.title: Veterans preference points in state and local government hiring
records.summary: Arizona adds preference points to your merit-system exam grade for state and local government jobs: five points for a Veteran, ten if you have a service-connected disability.
records.amount: 5 points, or 10 points with a service-connected disability
eligibility: You are a Veteran of the armed forces taking a merit-system employment exam for the state or a political subdivision
You must earn a passing grade without the preference first, then the points are added
A service-connected disability raises the preference to ten points
A spouse or surviving spouse of a Veteran who died of a service-connected disability gets the five-point preference
details: The points are added to a passing grade. They do not turn a failing exam into a passing one.
This applies to Arizona state government and to political subdivisions such as counties and cities that use a merit system.
The same statute gives a five-point preference to a person with a disability, separate from Veteran status.
records.agency: Arizona Department of Administration and local merit systems

records.title: Total property tax exemption on your home at a 100 percent rating
records.summary: A Veteran awarded 100 percent disability compensation with a rating of 100 percent disabled, or of individual unemployability, pays no property tax at all on the total appraised value of their residence homestead.
records.amount: The total appraised value of your residence homestead
eligibility: The VA has awarded you 100 percent disability compensation for a service-connected disability
And your rating is either 100 percent disabled or individual unemployability
The property must be your residence homestead as defined in Texas Tax Code Section 11.13
A surviving spouse may continue the exemption if the Veteran qualified at the time of death
details: Individual unemployability counts the same as a 100 percent schedular rating for this exemption. That catches a lot of Veterans who assume they do not qualify.
This is separate from and much larger than the partial exemption under Section 11.22. Check both.
Claimed through your county appraisal district, not the state.

records.title: Partial property tax exemption by disability rating
records.summary: Texas exempts part of the assessed value of a property you own on a sliding scale tied to your VA disability rating, from $5,000 at a 10 percent rating up to $12,000 at 70 percent or more.
records.amount: $5,000 to $12,000 of assessed value, by rating bracket
eligibility: 10 percent up to 30 percent rating: $5,000 of assessed value
30 percent up to 50 percent rating: $7,500
50 percent up to 70 percent rating: $10,000
70 percent and over: $12,000
You also get the full $12,000 if you are 65 or older with a rating of at least 10 percent, are totally blind in one or both eyes, or have lost the use of one or more limbs
A surviving spouse may be entitled to a portion of the exemption
details: You designate which property the exemption applies to. It does not have to be a homestead.
The age-65 provision matters: a 10 percent rating that is worth $5,000 before 65 is worth $12,000 after, which is a big jump that is easy to miss.
If you have a 100 percent rating or individual unemployability, look at the total homestead exemption under Section 11.131 instead, which is far larger.

records.title: Hazlewood Act tuition exemption
records.summary: Texas public colleges and universities must waive tuition and most required fees for qualifying Veterans, up to 150 credit hours. It is one of the most generous state education benefits in the country.
records.amount: Tuition and most required fees, up to 150 credit hours
eligibility: You currently reside in Texas
And you entered the service in Texas, declared Texas as your home of record, or would have been a Texas resident when you entered service
You were honorably discharged after more than 180 days of active duty, excluding training

You served during a qualifying period, which includes the national emergency that began September 11, 2001, the Persian Gulf War, Panama, Grenada and Lebanon, Vietnam, the Cold War, Korea, and both World Wars
details: The exemption covers tuition, dues, fees, and other required charges, including correspondence course fees. It specifically excludes general deposit fees, student services fees, and any charge for lodging, board, or clothing.
The cap is a cumulative 150 credit hours across all use of this exemption, not 150 hours per institution or per degree.
Related provisions in the same chapter extend the benefit to some spouses and children. Ask the institution's veteran services office about Hazlewood Legacy.
Apply through the financial aid or veteran services office at the Texas public institution you attend.
records.agency: Texas public institutions of higher education

records.title: Military employment preference for state agency jobs
records.summary: Texas state agencies must give hiring preference to Veterans and certain military family members over other applicants who are not better qualified, and every agency has a goal of Veterans making up at least 20 percent of its workforce.
records.amount: Hiring preference, plus a 20 percent Veteran workforce goal at every state agency
eligibility: A Veteran, including a Veteran with a disability
A Veteran's surviving spouse who has not remarried
An orphan of a Veteran killed while on active duty
The spouse of a member of the US armed forces or Texas National Guard serving on active duty

The spouse of a Veteran, where the spouse is the household's primary income and the Veteran has a total disability rating based on a service-connected disability of at least 70 percent or individual unemployability
details: The preference applies over other applicants for the same position who do not have a greater qualification. It is a tie-breaker in your favour, not an automatic hire.
The statute sets an order of priority: a Veteran with a disability first, then a Veteran, then a qualifying spouse, then a Veteran's surviving spouse.
Each state agency must set a goal of hiring Veterans into full-time positions equal to at least 20 percent of its total employees, and may set a higher goal.

records.title: Burial in a VA national cemetery
records.summary: Veterans, and in many cases their spouses and dependent children, can be buried in a VA national cemetery. Spouses remain eligible even if they remarried.
eligibility: Veterans who did not separate under dishonorable conditions
Service members who die while on active duty
Surviving spouses of Veterans, including those who have since remarried
Minor children, and unmarried adult dependent children, of Veterans
Special rules cover Reserve members, ROTC officers, NOAA and Public Health Service officers, WWII Merchant Mariners, Philippine Armed Forces Veterans, and Hmong Veterans
details: That surviving spouses stay eligible after remarrying surprises a lot of families, and it is worth knowing before making other arrangements.
Plan ahead. You can apply for a pre-need eligibility determination so your family is not making this decision under pressure.
Many states also run their own Veteran cemeteries with separate rules. Check your state page as well as this.
records.agency: US Department of Veterans Affairs, National Cemetery Administration

records.title: Post-9/11 GI Bill
records.summary: Pays the full cost of in-state tuition and fees at a public college, plus a monthly housing allowance and a books stipend. Up to 36 months of benefits, and for most Veterans it never expires.
records.amount: Up to 36 months. Full in-state public tuition and fees, plus housing and books.
eligibility: At least 90 days on active duty on or after 11 September 2001
Or you received a Purple Heart on or after that date and were honorably discharged
Or you served 30 continuous days and were discharged for a service-connected disability
Or you are a dependent using benefits transferred to you
details: Maximum entitlement is 36 months. Serving 56 months or more can open access to up to 48 months across combined programs.

IMPORTANT DEADLINE: if you were discharged before 1 January 2013, benefits expire 15 years after you separated. Discharged on or after that date, there is no expiration, thanks to the Forever GI Bill.
Full in-state tuition and fees at public schools. Private and foreign schools are capped at a set rate.
The monthly housing allowance is based on the cost of living where your school is located, and is not paid during school breaks.
It also funds tutoring, licensing and certification tests, and work-study.

records.title: VA disability compensation
records.summary: A tax-free monthly payment for an illness or injury caused or made worse by your military service. This is the benefit most other VA benefits key off, so it is usually the first thing to file for.
records.amount: Tax-free monthly payment, scaled to your disability rating
eligibility: You have a current illness or injury affecting your body or mind
And you served on active duty, active duty for training, or inactive duty training
And at least one applies: the condition began during service, service made a pre-existing condition worse, or a service-related disability appeared after discharge
An other than honorable, bad conduct, or dishonorable discharge may block eligibility, but a discharge upgrade or a VA Character of Discharge review can change that
details: Presumptive conditions are approved without you having to prove service caused them. These include a chronic illness appearing within one year of discharge, illnesses linked to toxic exposure, and conditions resulting from being a prisoner of war.
Covered conditions include chronic back pain, lung disease, hearing loss, PTSD, depression, and cancers linked to toxic exposure.
Rates change annually with a cost-of-living adjustment, so check the current rate table rather than relying on a figure you were quoted before.
Filing is free. An accredited Veterans Service Officer will help you file at no charge, and you should never pay a percentage of your back pay to anyone.

records.title: VA health care
records.summary: Enrolling in VA health care gives you access to VA medical centers and clinics nationwide. The PACT Act widened eligibility considerably, so it is worth re-checking even if you were turned down before.
eligibility: If you enlisted after 7 September 1980, or entered active duty after 16 October 1981, you generally need 24 continuous months of service or the full period you were called up
That requirement is waived if you were discharged for a service-connected disability, for a hardship, or under an early out
Reserve and National Guard members must have completed their full federal active-duty period
You must not have a dishonorable discharge. Other than honorable and bad conduct discharges may still qualify after a discharge upgrade or a Character of Discharge review
details: VA sorts enrollees into one of eight priority groups. Your group affects how quickly you enrol and what copays you pay.

You land in a higher priority group if you have a service-connected disability, are a post-9/11 combat Veteran, were a prisoner of war, hold a Purple Heart, or were exposed to toxins such as Agent Orange or asbestos.
The PACT Act extended eligibility to Veterans who served in Vietnam, the Gulf War, Iraq, Afghanistan, or any other combat zone after 9/11. If you were previously denied, apply again.

records.title: VA-backed home loan
records.summary: A VA guaranty lets a lender offer better terms than a conventional mortgage. Nearly 90 percent of VA-backed loans are made with no down payment at all.
records.amount: Nearly 90 percent of VA-backed loans are made with no down payment
eligibility: Veterans, service members, and some surviving spouses qualify based on service history and duty status
You need a Certificate of Eligibility to prove to a lender that you qualify
You still have to meet the lender's own credit and income requirements: the VA guarantees part of the loan, it does not lend the money
details: Four programs: purchase loans, Native American Direct Loans, interest rate reduction refinance loans, and cash-out refinance loans.
A VA funding fee usually applies, and some Veterans are exempt from it, including many with a service-connected disability. Ask before you assume you owe it.
The benefit is reusable. Using it once does not spend it forever.
Be cautious of refinance offers that arrive by mail or phone shortly after you close. Aggressive VA loan churning is a well-documented problem and it costs Veterans money.

records.title: Veteran Readiness and Employment (Chapter 31)
records.summary: If a service-connected disability limits your ability to work, VR&E helps you retrain, find work, or start a business. It is separate from the GI Bill and does not use up your GI Bill entitlement.
eligibility: You have a service-connected disability that limits your ability to work or prevents you from working
Eligibility is decided case by case with a Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor
details: Five tracks: returning to a former job, rapid access to employment, self-employment, long-term training services, and independent living for Veterans not currently able to work.
It also provides educational and career counselling.
Worth comparing against the GI Bill before you choose. VR&E is aimed at Veterans whose disability affects their capacity to work, and the two programs are separate entitlements.
